title: The Quiet Cost of a Campus App: Reading Trends, Comparisons and Proportions
instructions: 本材料为项目原创模拟场景、人物与数据，不是官方雅思试题，也未经考生难度标定。阅读全文后完成10题；区分原始说法、证据、推断与不确定事项。所有题干与选项为英文，解析为中文。填空按题目词数和原文词形作答。语法先学习规则，再完成8项独立新句或新数据练习。口语与写作迁移另用自己的新细节；完成本练习不等于独立能力已达标。
passage:
A. In September, a small university in the north of England began a twelve-week trial of a new campus app called CampusFlow. The app was designed to help students find empty study rooms, check library opening hours, and receive alerts about timetable changes. The project team, led by Dr. Helen Marsh, expected the app to reduce the time students spent searching for information. They also hoped it would lower the number of missed classes caused by last-minute room changes. The trial involved 1,200 students across three faculties: Science, Arts, and Business. At the start, 62% of participants said they used paper timetables or noticeboards as their main source of information. Only 18% used the university's existing website, and 20% relied on messages from friends. These baseline figures provided a clear picture of how students accessed information before the app was introduced, and they gave the team a reliable point of comparison for measuring later change.

B. By the end of the trial, the picture had changed considerably. The proportion of students using the app as their main source of information rose from 0% to 54%. Use of paper timetables and noticeboards fell sharply, from 62% to 21%. The website's share dropped slightly, from 18% to 15%, while reliance on friends' messages declined from 20% to 10%. Dr. Marsh noted that the app was most popular among first-year students: 71% of them used it daily, compared with 43% of second-year students and only 29% of final-year students. She suggested that final-year students had already developed reliable personal networks and therefore felt less need for a central tool. This pattern suggests that the app's value may be highest for those who are new to the university environment, since they have fewer established habits and contacts to rely on.

C. The team also measured missed classes. In the twelve weeks before the trial, the three faculties recorded an average of 84 missed classes per week due to room changes. During the trial, this figure fell to 57 per week. However, the improvement was not equal across faculties. Science saw the largest drop, from 31 to 14 missed classes per week. Arts fell from 28 to 22, and Business from 25 to 21. Dr. Marsh warned that these numbers should be treated with caution. "The autumn term is always quieter than the spring term," she said. "We cannot assume that the app alone caused the fall." Other factors, such as the time of year and the specific courses running, could also have influenced attendance. For example, the autumn term may include fewer field trips or practical sessions that are easily disrupted by room changes, so part of the improvement may reflect the normal seasonal pattern rather than the app itself.

D. Student feedback revealed hidden assumptions in the project's original design. The team had assumed that all students owned smartphones with reliable internet access. In fact, 9% of participants reported that their phones often lost connection in older buildings. The team had also assumed that students would check the app before every class. Interviews showed that many students checked it only once a day, usually in the morning. One Business student explained, "I look at it with breakfast. After that, I'm too busy." Another assumption was that clearer information would automatically lead to better attendance. Yet several Arts students said they missed classes because of part-time jobs, not because they were confused about rooms. These findings highlight the gap between designers' expectations and students' actual daily routines, and they show why testing a tool with real users matters.

E. The app's usage statistics showed a clear weekly pattern. Activity was highest on Mondays, when 68% of users opened the app at least once. It declined steadily through the week, reaching 41% on Fridays. Weekend use was very low, at 12% on Saturdays and 9% on Sundays. The team found this trend unsurprising, since most classes take place on weekdays. However, they were surprised by the age difference: students aged 18 to 20 used the app almost twice as often as students aged 25 and over. The older group reported that they preferred email reminders, which they could read on larger screens. This preference suggests that communication channels may need to be tailored to different age groups rather than relying on a single app for everyone.

F. The final report recommended three changes. First, the app should work offline, storing the latest timetable on the phone. Second, the team should send a single daily email summary to students who prefer email. Third, the university should collect better data on why students miss classes, separating room confusion from other reasons such as work or illness. Dr. Marsh concluded, "A useful tool is not the same as a complete solution. We need to compare what we hoped would happen with what actually happened." The university will decide in January whether to continue the app for all 8,000 students, and the trial results will form the main evidence for that decision.

questions.prompt: According to paragraph A, what percentage of participants used paper timetables or noticeboards as their main source of information at the start?
questions.explanation: 原文A段明确说“62% of participants said they used paper timetables or noticeboards as their main source of information”。
questions.evidence: At the start, 62% of participants said they used paper timetables or noticeboards as their main source of information.

questions.prompt: Which year group had the highest rate of daily use?
questions.explanation: 比较同一指标下的三个年级：71%、43%、29%。年龄分组的使用频率不是同一分组，故不混成一个排名题。
questions.evidence: Dr. Marsh noted that the app was most popular among first-year students: 71% of them used it daily, compared with 43% of second-year students and only 29% of final-year students.

questions.prompt: In which faculty did missed classes fall by the largest number per week?
questions.explanation: C段给出Science从31降到14（减少17），Arts从28降到22（减少6），Business从25降到21（减少4），所以Science降幅最大。
questions.evidence: Science saw the largest drop, from 31 to 14 missed classes per week.

questions.prompt: What does Dr. Marsh say about the fall in missed classes?
options: It proves the app works well.
It was caused by part-time jobs.
It may be partly caused by the season.
It was the same in all faculties.
answers: It may be partly caused by the season.
questions.explanation: C段Dr. Marsh说“The autumn term is always quieter than the spring term”并说“We cannot assume that the app alone caused the fall”，说明下降可能部分由季节造成。
questions.evidence: "The autumn term is always quieter than the spring term," she said. "We cannot assume that the app alone caused the fall."

questions.prompt: Which assumption is challenged by the connection problems?
options: Every class would use the same room.
All students would have reliable internet access.
All absences would be recorded in the app.
answers: All students would have reliable internet access.
questions.explanation: 团队假设所有学生都能可靠联网，但9%的参与者反映手机在旧楼经常断网，因此受到挑战的是 All students would have reliable internet access。
questions.evidence: The team had assumed that all students owned smartphones with reliable internet access. In fact, 9% of participants reported that their phones often lost connection in older buildings.

questions.prompt: On which day was app activity highest?
questions.explanation: E段说“Activity was highest on Mondays, when 68% of users opened the app at least once.”
questions.evidence: Activity was highest on Mondays, when 68% of users opened the app at least once.

questions.prompt: According to paragraph E, how did students aged 25 and over prefer to receive reminders?
questions.explanation: E段说“The older group reported that they preferred email reminders, which they could read on larger screens.”
questions.evidence: The older group reported that they preferred email reminders, which they could read on larger screens.

questions.prompt: Complete with ONE NUMBER AND A SYMBOL from the passage: Weekend use was 12% on Saturdays and ______ on Sundays.
questions.explanation: 周日比例为9%；12%为周六，68%为周一。须保留%来表示比例。
questions.evidence: Weekend use was very low, at 12% on Saturdays and 9% on Sundays.

questions.prompt: Complete using ONE WORD from paragraph F: For offline use, the app should store the latest ______ on the phone.
questions.explanation: 离线功能的具体缓存内容是timetable；未说缓存所有数据。
questions.evidence: First, the app should work offline, storing the latest timetable on the phone.

questions.prompt: The university has already decided to make CampusFlow available to all students.
questions.explanation: 文中说将在January决定是否向全部8,000人推广，说明尚未作出这项决定。
questions.evidence: The university will decide in January whether to continue the app for all 8,000 students, and the trial results will form the main evidence for that decision.

grammar.title: 数据句的时态、比较、百分比与百分点
grammar.explanation: 复习：明确结束的过去时间用一般过去时；from说明起点，to说明终点，by说明变化量。本课新增：比例从8%到12%增加4个百分点，却是相对原比例增加50%，percent与percentage points不能互换。比较比例须保持分母和指标可比，不能因人数相同就说比例相同。twice that at...可避免把比例同地点直接比较。the proportion/percentage作主语通常按单数处理。描述变化延续至今可用现在完成时。compared with和compared to在很多比较语境均可用，than后省略重复动词也可能正确；不把合法变体当错项。先后变化不自动证明因果，要保留证据限制。以下均为新模拟数据句。
grammar.example: The proportion of students using the app as their main source of information rose from 0% to 54%.

questions.prompt: Choose the standard sentence about a completed past month.
options: The number of visitors has rose by 20% last month.
The number of visitors is rise by 20% last month.
The number of visitors rises by 20% last month.
The number of visitors rose by 20% last month.
answers: The number of visitors rose by 20% last month.
questions.explanation: last month是结束的过去时间，用rose；其余有时态或动词形式错误。
questions.evidence: The number of visitors rose by 20% last month.

questions.prompt: A share rose from 20% to 30%. Which change is accurate?
questions.explanation: 30%-20%=10个百分点；相对增幅是10/20=50%，不能把10个百分点写成10%。
questions.evidence: The share rose from 20% to 30%, an increase of 10 percentage points.

questions.prompt: A visitor count rose from 200 to 300. What was the relative increase?
questions.explanation: 增量100除以原数200=50%。33%近似误用终值作分母。
questions.evidence: The visitor count rose by 50 percent, from 200 to 300.

questions.prompt: At Site A, 40% of visitors cycled; at Site B, 20% cycled. Which statement compares the shares accurately?
options: The share at Site A was twice that at Site B.
The share at Site B was twice that at Site A.
The shares were equal because both sites had cyclists.
Site A had twice as many visitors as Site B.
answers: The share at Site A was twice that at Site B.
questions.explanation: 40%是20%的两倍；比例不能推出访客总人数之比。that替代the share，使比较对象一致。
questions.evidence: The share at Site A was twice that at Site B.

questions.prompt: Complete the change accurately: The number fell ______ 70, from 420 to 350.
questions.evidence: The number fell by 70, from 420 to 350.

questions.prompt: Choose the standard past-tense form: The proportion of participants who reported delays ______ lower in 2024 than in 2023.
questions.explanation: 主句中心主语是单数the proportion；who reported delays修饰participants，不改变单数一致。
questions.evidence: The proportion of participants who reported delays was lower in 2024 than in 2023.

questions.prompt: Use the present perfect: Since the trial began, the share using bicycles ______ from 12% to 18%.
questions.explanation: 单数share用has，完成时用过去分词risen；题目指定现在完成时。
questions.evidence: Since the trial began, the share using bicycles has risen from 12% to 18%.

questions.prompt: Reports of falls declined during a campaign, but there was no control group. Which sentence keeps the causal claim appropriately limited?
options: The campaign must have prevented every unreported accident.
The figures confirm that every other influence stayed unchanged.
Reports fell during the campaign, but these figures alone do not show that it caused the fall.
The campaign is proved to be the only possible cause of the fall.
answers: Reports fell during the campaign, but these figures alone do not show that it caused the fall.
questions.explanation: 同期变化不能单独证明因果，无对照时还可能有其他解释。Reports fell during the campaign, but these figures alone do not show that it caused the fall 区分了观察结果与因果结论。
questions.evidence: Reports fell during the campaign, but these figures alone do not show that it caused the fall.

part1: Do you often use apps on your phone?
What kind of information do you look for online?

speaking.part2: Describe a time when a new tool or app was introduced at your school or workplace. You should say: what the tool was; who used it; what changed after it was introduced; and explain whether you think it was a success.
part3: Why do some people prefer email to apps for reminders?
What problems can happen when a new technology is introduced?
Should universities collect more data about student attendance? Why?
How can we compare the real effects of a new tool with its expected effects?

transfer.writing: You are a student representative. Write a short report (about 150 words) for the university about a new campus app. Describe one trend, one comparison between two groups, and one proportion. Then explain one hidden assumption the project team made and suggest one improvement. Use accurate past and present tenses.
